_doc: Scenes and narration of the Graft explainer. One entry per scene; each language is a list of sentences (cues). Write numbers in words. Then run narrate.py on this folder. Every organisation, person and pull request shown is fictional.

en: This is Graft.
It adds intent review and policy checks to pull requests written by coding agents.
Coding agents now open pull requests faster than people can review them.
Reviewers read every diff, line by line.
And the description they start from was written by the agent being judged.
Graft works with three roles.
The agent writes the code.
The reviewer decides what merges.
The platform owner sets the rules.
All of it runs on top of GitHub, with nothing to migrate.
When a pull request opens, GitHub sends a signed webhook.
The server verifies it, removes duplicates, and queues a job.
The worker reads everything again from the GitHub API, and never trusts the webhook payload.
It publishes three check runs and one managed comment.
First answer: who wrote it.
Agents add Graft trailers to their commits, and a git hook can add them automatically.
Bot accounts and agent co-authors count too.
The reviewer sees the agent, the model, the task, and the session.
Second answer: what it claims to do.
A writer model drafts an intent card.
A second model, the verifier, sees only the diff and the card, and checks every claim.
The pull request text is treated as data, never as instructions.
Third answer: how risky it is.
Fixed rules over paths, size, tests, CI, auth, and migrations set a risk floor.
A model can raise the class, but never lower it.
Fourth answer: what the policy says.
The repository's graft dot yaml file is read from the base branch only.
A block wins first, then a require, and then an approve.
This changes the reviewer's day.
They read the card before the diff.
Trivial changes could flow on their own, and sensitive ones go to the right people.
Agents keep working as before, plus a few trailers.
Reviewers rate each card, so its accuracy is measured.
Graft never stores file contents, diffs, or pull request text.
It keeps paths, commit hashes, and numbers.
Today it runs in shadow mode: every check is neutral.
Enforcement comes only after the cards prove ninety percent accurate.
Read the card before you read the diff.
Graft runs offline in under five minutes.
Start with the documentation.
